test_title: PYST 46 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 29 Nov, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech.

She told me that she had been learning French for three months.

options.text: She said to me, "I am learning French for three months."
She said to me, "I have been learning French for three months."
She said to me, "I had learnt French for three months."
She said to me, "I learnt French for three months."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reported Speech:** She told me that she had been learning French for three months.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"She had been learning" becomes "I have been learning"**
 
 
• Indirect speech tense (past perfect continuous) is converted to direct speech tense (present perfect continuous).
 
• Pronoun "she" is changed to "I" for direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"French for three months" remains unchanged**
 
 
• The time duration does not change in conversion.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "She told me"
 
• Converted to: "She said to me," which is appropriate for direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period ".".
 
• Reporting clause follows the quoted speech, separated by a comma.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said to me, "I have been learning French for three months.""*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said to me, "I am learning French for three months.""
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "am learning" does not match the original past perfect continuous tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** "She said to me, "I had learnt French for three months.""
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "had learnt" changes the meaning to past perfect, indicating a completed action, which is inconsistent with the original continuous action.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said to me, "I learnt French for three months.""
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "learnt" changes the meaning to simple past, losing the continuous aspect of the action.
